answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to earn trust through a public beacon: a slowly accumulated record of useful work that peers verify and stake on. A fresh account starts as a faint ember with no history, so it cannot vote, claim rewards, or borrow reputation until it has completed real tasks over time. Like a mesa, that record is hard to fake at scale — copying one profile is easy, but forging thousands of long, distinct histories costs more than any single payout, so floods of fake identities stand out and get throttled.
